item: A refused or failed rebuild of sources leaves the store as found, the derived view included (audit 0.5.0 A-012, routing 11)
refs: audit 0.5.0 A-012; follows PR #1489 and R205
summary: upgrade_sources_to_composite_key dropped keyword_mentions_all first and decided its schema refusals afterwards, so a store holding a column this build does not know was refused with the view gone, and ensure_source_composite_key recreates the view only after a success: every query on keyword_mentions_all failed until the next boot (reproduced: view present before, 0 after the refusal). The refusals that the schema alone decides (unknown column, required column without default, with feed_key counted as present because it is added next) and the read of the extra indexes and triggers now run before the pragma and before any statement that changes the store; the one read that must follow the column being added (old_cols, which decides what is copied) stays after it; the DROP VIEW moved inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so a failure after it rolls it back with the rest (SQLite DDL is transactional). This is routing 11's two-phase read, and it is also the only part of A-012 that was a defect and not a hardening: the loop heads in this function were already moved out by R205. tests/test_composite_key_leaves_the_store_as_found.py: refusal leaves the view and the legacy state; the statement trace shows no PRAGMA foreign_keys, DROP, ALTER, CREATE, INSERT, UPDATE or BEGIN before a refusal; a failed copy rolls the view back; a successful rebuild still ends with the view; a table lacking only feed_key is not refused. Three of the five fail without the change. Not changed: the Alembic revision that calls the function (same signature and returns), the order of the other boot steps.
